previous_admission_summary.summary_paragraph: The patient was admitted due to malfunction of her hemodialysis catheter, which failed despite initial replacement and tPA treatment. A new tunneled catheter was successfully placed, restoring dialysis access. During admission, she was found to have infected calciphylaxis wounds with polymicrobial growth including Pseudomonas, prompting a 10-day course of ciprofloxacin and clindamycin. Her severe hyperparathyroidism (PTH 1110) was confirmed as a driver of calciphylaxis, and she was scheduled for surgical evaluation for parathyroidectomy. Left heel pain was evaluated with X-ray, showing no fracture but findings consistent with plantar fasciitis. She was discharged to an extended care facility on antibiotics and with wound care instructions, to continue dialysis and follow up with surgery.
problems: Mechanical complication of other vascular device, implant, and graft
Pseudomonas infection in conditions classified elsewhere and of unspecified site
